That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

answer.rationale: Two of the three symptoms are funnel-internal: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly addresses both, whereas activation_messaging treats the downstream symptom only. The competitor's entry pricing is real, but promotional_pricing buys volume at the cost of price integrity and tends to attract the least durable cohort, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue; referral_incentive and enterprise_sales_assist target segments that are not where the current degradation is showing. So I am provisionally confirming leadership's direction. My single verification goes to memory_86, because it is the load-bearing evidence for that direction and the one I am about to act on: it is the memory that claims shortening onboarding lifts completion and time-to-value. I specifically want to know whether the original record measured downstream retained/qualified revenue or only completion-rate lift, and whether it ran on the same self-serve population now under competitive pressure. I did not verify memory_31 because it is a partially redundant confirmation of the same lever (signup-field reduction), so it cannot overturn the choice; and I did not verify memory_73 because even a strong pricing result would not change my ranking, given the sustainability constraint. If memory_86 turns out to be a completion-metric-only result with no revenue linkage, I would drop to memory_31's narrower signup-field change or reconsider activation_messaging.
